body:
### Problem

When the evaluated statusline-format string is wider than `maxwidth` and contains double-width (CJK) characters, the truncation in `build_stl_str_hl()` can leave the result without a terminating NUL at the right place. The returned string then has stale bytes from the pre-truncation buffer appended, starting in the middle of a multibyte character, i.e. **invalid UTF-8**.

Trigger: truncation removes from the start (`<` case), the remaining width is one cell short because a double-width character had to be dropped (`width + 1 < maxwidth`), so the "Fill up for half a double-wide character" loop runs. That loop writes the fill char at the old end of the string and never writes a NUL afterwards (the original NUL was just overwritten).

Real-world impact: with the default `'titlestring'` and `'title'` enabled, opening a file with a long Japanese path makes every UI attached via `--embed` receive a `set_title` event whose string is not valid UTF-8. MessagePack consumers that validate strings (e.g. VimR, see https://github.com/qvacua/vimr/issues/1172) fail to decode the whole redraw batch. Observed `set_title` value looks like:

`<` + (valid tail of the title) + ` ` + `<stale bytes starting with a continuation byte, e.g. 0x88>` + ... + ` - Nvim`, with length larger than the valid title.

Code (v0.12.5, `src/nvim/statusline.c`, `build_stl_str_hl()`, ~L1990-2045):

```c
      char *end = out + outputlen;
      ...
      memmove(trunc_p + 1, trunc_end_p, (size_t)(end - trunc_end_p) + 1);  // +1 for NUL
      end -= (size_t)(trunc_end_p - (trunc_p + 1));
      *trunc_p = '<';
      ...
      if (width + 1 < maxwidth) {
        // Advance the pointer to the end of the string
        trunc_p = end;
      }

      // Fill up for half a double-wide character.
      while (++width < maxwidth) {
        schar_get_adv(&trunc_p, fillchar);
        end = trunc_p;
      }
      (void)end;          // <-- nothing ever writes NUL at trunc_p / end
```

`(void)end;` discards the updated end. (Similar to Vim, where the same logic appears; I did not test Vim.)

### Steps to reproduce

Minimal, Nvim only (`nvim --clean --headless -l min.lua`):

```lua
local function valid(s) -- strict UTF-8 check
  local i, n = 1, #s
  while i <= n do
    local c = s:byte(i)
    local k = c < 0x80 and 0 or (c >= 0xC2 and c <= 0xDF) and 1 or (c >= 0xE0 and c <= 0xEF) and 2 or (c >= 0xF0 and c <= 0xF4) and 3 or nil
    if not k then return false end
    for j = 1, k do local d = s:byte(i + j); if not d or d < 0x80 or d > 0xBF then return false end end
    i = i + 1 + k
  end
  return true
end
local s = vim.api.nvim_eval_statusline("%{'あいうえおかきくけこ'}", { maxwidth = 8 })
print(vim.inspect(s.str), "valid UTF-8:", valid(s.str))
```

Actual output on 0.12.5:

```
"<くけこ <88>おかきくけこ" valid UTF-8: false
```

(a `<`, three kana, the fill space, then stale bytes of the untruncated string starting with continuation byte `0x88`).
Even `maxwidth` hits it (odd `maxwidth` does not), because 20 cells cannot be cut to exactly 8 with 2-cell characters.

Via a UI (`'title'` + default `'titlestring'` + long CJK path), script `repro.py` (below) (`uv run --with msgpack repro.py /opt/homebrew/bin/nvim`): attaches with `nvim --clean --embed`, `:set title`, `:edit /tmp/日本語テスト/とても長い日本語のディレクトリ名その1/…その2/…その3/メモ.txt` and reads raw `set_title` bytes for UI widths 20..120. Result on 0.12.5: 7 of 51 widths give invalid UTF-8 (e.g. `columns=28`, 219 bytes, ending in `...その3) - Nvim` after stale bytes). With `:set titlelen=0` or `:set titlestring=%t`: 0 of 51.

<details><summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
# Run: uv run --with msgpack repro.py [/path/to/nvim]
# Attach a UI to `nvim --clean --embed` and look at the raw bytes of `set_title`
# for several UI widths (the result depends on 'columns' / 'titlelen').
import os, select, subprocess, sys, time, msgpack

nvim = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "nvim"
d = "/tmp/日本語テスト/" + "/".join("とても長い日本語のディレクトリ名その%d" % i for i in (1, 2, 3))
os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
path = d + "/メモ.txt"
open(path, "w").write("x\n")

def last_title(cols, extra=()):
    p = subprocess.Popen([nvim, "--clean", "--embed"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
    u = msgpack.Unpacker(raw=True)  # raw=True: no UTF-8 validation on our side
    calls = [("nvim_ui_attach", [cols, 40, {"ext_linegrid": True, "rgb": True}]),
             ("nvim_command", ["set title"])]
    calls += [("nvim_command", [c]) for c in extra] + [("nvim_command", ["edit " + path])]
    for i, (m, a) in enumerate(calls, 1):
        p.stdin.write(msgpack.packb([0, i, m, a])); p.stdin.flush()
    title, end = b"", time.time() + 1.5
    while time.time() < end:
        if select.select([p.stdout], [], [], 0.1)[0]:
            u.feed(os.read(p.stdout.fileno(), 65536))
            for m in u:
                if m[0] == 2 and m[1] == b"redraw":
                    for ev in m[2]:
                        if ev[0] == b"set_title":
                            title = ev[-1][0]; end = min(end, time.time() + 0.15)
    p.kill()
    return title

def check(t):
    try:
        t.decode("utf-8"); return "ok"
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return "INVALID UTF-8"

bad = []
for cols in range(20, 121, 2):
    t = last_title(cols)
    if check(t) != "ok":
        bad.append((cols, t))
print("default titlestring: %d of 51 widths produced invalid UTF-8" % len(bad))
for cols, t in bad[:3]:
    print(" columns=%d len=%d tail=%r" % (cols, len(t), t[-24:]))
for label, extra in [("titlelen=0", ["set titlelen=0"]), ("titlestring=%t", ["set titlestring=%t"])]:
    n = sum(check(last_title(c, extra)) != "ok" for c in range(20, 121, 2))
    print("%-16s %d of 51 invalid" % (label, n))
```

</details>

### Expected behavior

The result is always a valid, NUL-terminated string of at most `maxwidth` cells; `set_title` always carries valid UTF-8.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.12.5, Release build (Homebrew)

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

Not tested.

### Operating system/version

macOS (Apple Silicon, arm64)

### Terminal name/version

n/a (embedded UI via `--embed`; also reproduced headless with `nvim_eval_statusline`)

### $TERM environment variable

n/a

### Installation

homebrew

### Additional notes

- **Already fixed on master, by accident?** The logic was moved into `stl_truncate()` by #40369 ("feat(statusline)!: allow %= in item groups, scope %< to item groups", merged 2026-06-27). It ends with `**out_p = NUL;`, and `out_p` is advanced by the fill loop, so the bug should be gone there. I could not run a master build; this is from reading the code only. `release-0.12` does not contain the change (no `**out_p = NUL`), so 0.12.x is still affected. Request: backport a minimal fix to `release-0.12` (write `*trunc_p = NUL` after the fill loop), if 0.12.x patch releases are still planned.
- Workarounds: `:set titlelen=0`, or `:set titlestring=%t`, or `:set notitle`.
- Related client-side issue (client stops processing after the invalid string): https://github.com/qvacua/vimr/issues/1172
- Searched for duplicates (titlelen, set_title utf-8, statusline truncate/garbage, nvim_eval_statusline): none found.

comment_data.body:
>  **Already fixed on master, by accident?** The logic was moved into `stl_truncate()`

Well, simplifying the logic does tend to accidentally fix latent bugs. I don't think we plan to fix this in 0.12.x

title: Statusline/`'titlestring'` truncation with `maxwidth` leaves unterminated buffer: invalid UTF-8 in `set_title` (and `nvim_eval_statusline()`)
